I am 73, farming only 3 mu by myself, so this year I will keep things simple, stable, and not too labor-heavy. I will put 1 mu into cotton and keep 2 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because that matches the way I already farm and spreads my risk. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on it to protect yield, but I will not push inputs too hard because my land is small and I care more about steady harvests than chasing the highest output. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, give moderate fertilizer, irrigate twice, and manage weeds and disease with limited spraying. After wheat harvest, I will put those same 2 mu into hybrid maize, using no-tillage to save labor and time. For cotton, I will use an improved seed, keep fertilizer balanced, irrigate a few times, and spray more than wheat and maize because cotton usually needs closer pest control. My goal is a manageable year with reliable grain for income and a cotton crop that is worth the work.
